note: Hypothetical lunar base building types. Figures come from CLAUDE-Moon-Data-Sources.md §10–11. Tags: K = contract value or NASA requirement, C = company claim, M = measured or flown, E = independent estimate, D = derived here, ASSUMP = illustrative assumption. A null default means unknown (never zero): users may enter a value.

lifeSupport.source: NASA Baseline Values and Assumptions Document (BVAD) Rev 2: oxygen 0.84 kg, drinking water 2.0 + food water 0.5 kg, food 1.83 kg per crew member per day

transportCases.label: Optimistic
transportCases.note: 4 tankers at $10M a launch, 100 t landed, reused lander

transportCases.label: Central
transportCases.note: 10 tankers at $50M a launch, 50 t landed, lander expended (+$100M)

transportCases.label: Conservative
transportCases.note: 20 tankers at $100M a launch, 15 t landed, reused lander

buildings.label: Crew habitat
buildings.description: Pressurised living quarters with life support. Crew breathe oxygen, drink and use water and eat food every day; recycling cuts how much must be made locally or shipped from Earth.

params.label: Crew
params.note: Foundation Surface Habitat: 4 crew, short stays.

params.label: Power demand
params.note: No published figure for the Foundation Surface Habitat: an illustrative load for life support, thermal control and equipment.

params.label: Water recycled
params.note: Share of used water reclaimed (urine, sweat, humidity). The ISS reached 98% in 2023.

params.label: Oxygen regenerated
params.note: Share of breathed oxygen recovered from exhaled CO₂. Today's stations recover part of it.

params.label: Stored reserves
params.note: Oxygen, water and food stored on site to bridge gaps between deliveries.

params.label: Landed mass
params.note: Foundation Surface Habitat landed-mass limit.

buildings.label: Vertical solar array
buildings.description: Solar panels on a tall mast. They produce power only while the Sun is up, so output depends on how much of the time the site is lit.

params.label: Rated output
params.note: VSAT: 10 kW per array (a 50 kW class also exists).

params.label: Surveyed sunlit fraction
params.note: Leave blank to use the site model: 0.5 on flat ground away from the poles. Near the poles it depends on terrain: ridges are lit 0.7–0.9 of the time (LOLA illumination maps), crater floors never.

params.label: Mast height
params.note: At least 5 m, goal 10 m: height lifts panels above nearby shadows near the poles.

buildings.label: Fission surface power
buildings.description: A small nuclear reactor: steady power day and night for about ten years. Crewed buildings must stay outside its radiation keep-out.

params.label: Electrical output
params.note: 40 kWe for 10 years (a 2025 directive asks for at least 100 kWe).

params.label: Radiation keep-out
params.note: Dose at most 5 rem/yr above background at 1 km: crewed buildings stay outside.

params.label: Landed mass
params.note: At most 6,000 kg.

buildings.label: Night power storage
buildings.description: Stores daytime solar energy and releases it through the lunar night, which lasts about two weeks away from the poles.

params.label: Usable capacity
params.note: 10 kW through a 200-hour night = 2,000 kWh.

params.label: Maximum output
params.note: Power the fuel cell can deliver at once.

params.label: Landed mass
params.note: No public figure. Enter one if known; otherwise its delivery cost stays unknown.

buildings.label: Ice mining plant
buildings.description: Heats icy regolith from permanently shadowed craters and collects the water. Water can be drunk, or split into oxygen and hydrogen.

params.label: Water produced
params.note: 2.78 kg of water an hour (thermal extraction estimate).

params.label: Energy per kg
params.note: 2.6 kWh of heat + 0.25 kWh of electricity per kg, all supplied as electricity here.

params.label: Landed mass
params.note: No public figure. Enter one if known.

buildings.label: Oxygen plant
buildings.description: Extracts oxygen from lunar soil. Mare basalts are rich in ilmenite (FeTiO₃), the easiest mineral to reduce; highlands need more energy-hungry processes.

params.label: Oxygen produced
params.note: Production target.

params.label: Energy per kg
params.note: Ilmenite reduction: 24.3 ± 5.8 kWh per kg at 10 wt% ilmenite. Molten regolith electrolysis ~21; carbothermal ~75 in the lab.

params.label: Landed mass
params.note: No public figure. Enter one if known.

buildings.label: Greenhouse
buildings.description: Grows food under artificial light and releases oxygen as the plants photosynthesise. Every figure here is illustrative: no lunar greenhouse has public specifications.

params.label: Growing area
params.note: Area under LED lighting.

params.label: Power per m²
params.note: Lighting, pumps and climate control.

params.label: Food per m²
params.note: Edible food harvested per m² per day.

params.label: Oxygen per m²
params.note: Oxygen released by the plants per m² per day.

params.label: Landed mass
params.note: No public figure. Enter one if known.

buildings.label: Landing pad
buildings.example: Sintered regolith pad for a 100 t lander
buildings.description: A hardened pad so landers do not blast regolith across the base. Rocket plumes still throw ejecta for kilometres, so other buildings keep their distance.

params.label: Pad diameter
params.note: About three times the lander's footprint (NASA/Purdue 2025).

params.label: Plume keep-out
params.note: NASA keeps surface vehicles ~2 km away during landings.

params.label: Landed mass
params.note: Sintered from local regolith; the equipment's mass is not public.
